title: Spatial proteomic profiling of tonsil cancer microenvironments using deep visual proteomics
author: Zheng, Mund, et al.
materials:
1.Antibody panel: Centrifuge the tubes of fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)/phycoerythrin (PE)/allophycocyanin (APC)-conjugated antibodies (Miltenyi Biotec, see key resources table) at 13,000 × g for 5 min at 22°C–26°C.
Alternatives: FITC can be substituted with Vio B515, while Vio R667 may replace APC (spectrally similar).
Note: Carefully pipette the supernatant to prevent potential aggregates that may cause staining artifacts.
Note: Antibody staining optimization is Critical for robust cyclic immunofluorescence on the MACSima platform. Miltenyi optimizes its pre-conjugated antibodies (FITC, PE, APC) for photostability and cyclic imaging under standardized protocols. External vendor antibodies must match MACSima-compatible fluorophores and undergo validation in FFPE tissues. Key steps include testing specificity against single-plex controls or knockout tissues, screening for cross-reactivity in multiplex panels and titrating concentrations to balance signal-to-noise ratios. This validation process ensures compatibility with cyclic imaging, minimizes artifacts, and preserves spatial proteomic accuracy.
2.Microtome (HM 355S): Set the desired section thickness, check cooling if applicable, and perform a test section to verify smooth operation.
Note: Before use, clean the microtome thoroughly, secure a sharp blade, and mount the specimen block parallel to the blade.
Alternatives: Other rotary microtomes (e.g., Leica RM2255 or Thermo Fisher HM 325) may be used if they support equivalent section thickness precision (1–10 μm) and specimen cooling.
3.MACSima imaging platform (Miltenyi Biotec): Calibrate the system using control tissues to optimize multiplexed staining and imaging conditions.
Alternatives: Our pilot data (n=3 colorectal cancer tissues) suggests cyclic immunofluorescence (CyCIF) with fluorophore bleaching (4.5% H2O2/24 mM NaOH in PBS, 1 hour at 22°C–26°C under white light)2 may substitute MACSima for ≤4-cycle staining (around 12-plex), but requires post-bleaching antibody revalidation and image registration tools (e.g., ASHLAR3) for alignment.
4.Laser microdissection system (LMD7, Leica): Align reference masks (.XML) to ensure precise laser microdissection for downstream analyses.
Alternatives: The CellCut system (MMI) can substitute the Leica LMD7 for microdissection and collection of cell contours.4
5.Mass spectrometry setup: Configure the Evosep One LC system (Evosep) coupled to a timsTOF SCP mass spectrometer (Bruker) for proteomics.
Note: Regular maintenance of both the LC and mass spectrometer, include cleaning the ion source and tuning the instrument to ensure optimal sensitivity and mass accuracy.
Alternatives: The nanoLC systems (e.g., Thermo Ultimate 3000 or Vanquish UHPLC systems) can replace Evosep One if adjusted for low-flow (100 nL/min) gradients.
Alternatives: The timsTOF SCP is replaceable with other high-sensitivity DIA-MS instruments (e.g., Orbitrap Astral) but requires setting re-optimization.1
6.Software installation: Install and configure these required programs: MACS iQ View, BIAS, DIA-NN, and FragPipe (see key resources table).
Alternatives: For image analysis, open-source tools including DeepCell can substitute MACS iQ View for tasks including segmentation, though they lack native compatibility with MACSima's proprietary cyclic imaging data formats.5 For proteomics analysis, Spectronaut (Biognosys) may replace DIA-NN for DIA data processing but require manual parameter optimization and may yield slightly different peptide identification rates.

steps.title: Centrifuge antibody panels
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes of FITC/PE/APC‑conjugated antibodies at 13,000 × g for 5 min at 22 °C–26 °C and carefully pipette off the supernatant to avoid aggregates.

steps.title: Prepare microtome and cut sections
steps.instruction: Set the microtome (e.g., HM 355S) to the desired thickness (1–10 µm), verify cooling, perform a test section, clean the instrument, install a sharp blade, and mount the FFPE block parallel to the blade.

steps.title: Calibrate MACSima imaging system
steps.instruction: Run the MACSima platform calibration using control tissues to optimise multiplexed staining and imaging conditions; optionally perform FITC/PE/APC photobleaching with 4.5 % H₂O₂/24 mM NaOH in PBS for 1 h at 22 °C–26 °C under white light if using a CyCIF alternative.

steps.title: Align laser microdissection masks
steps.instruction: Load the reference mask (.XML) into the Leica LMD7 (or CellCut) and align it to ensure precise laser microdissection of downstream regions.

steps.title: Configure LC‑MS instrumentation
steps.instruction: Set up the Evosep One LC coupled to a timsTOF SCP mass spectrometer (or equivalent low‑flow nanoLC and high‑sensitivity DIA‑MS instrument) and perform routine cleaning of the ion source and tuning for optimal sensitivity.

steps.title: Install required analysis software
steps.instruction: Install and configure MACS iQ View, BIAS, DIA‑NN, and FragPipe (or approved alternatives such as DeepCell, Spectronaut).

steps.title: Pre‑treat PEN membrane slides
steps.instruction: Expose PEN slides to UV for 1 h; immerse in acetone for 5 min; immerse in Vectabond (1:50 in acetone) for 5 min; rinse in distilled water for 30 s; air‑dry 12–18 h (handle acetone and Vectabond in a fume hood).

steps.title: Section FFPE tissue onto slides
steps.instruction: Cut 3 µm sections, mount them in the lower half of the PEN slides within the rectangular guide area, then bake at 37 °C for 12–18 h.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and rehydrate slides
steps.instruction: Bake slides at 60 °C for 20 min; sequentially immerse in 3 × 5 min xylene, 2 × 2 min 100 % ethanol, 2 min 95 % ethanol, 2 min 80 % ethanol, 2 min 70 % ethanol, and 2 min ddH₂O (use fume hood; keep slides hydrated).

steps.title: Heat‑induced epitope retrieval
steps.instruction: Heat slides in EDTA buffer containing 10 % glycerol at 88 °C for 45 min in a water bath; mount slides in the MACSima two‑well frame; add 550 µL running buffer; incubate with 1 µg/mL DAPI (1:5 dilution) in the dark at 22 °C–26 °C for 10 min; wash three times with running buffer; add a final 550 µL running buffer. Store slides in running buffer at 4 °C for ≤1 week.

steps.title: Create antibody worksheet for cyclic IF
steps.instruction: Complete the antibody worksheet (Document S1) by entering experiment background, marking the two‑well frame area, specifying exposure times (APC 6/36/216 ms, PE 5/20/80 ms, FITC 8/32/128 ms), filling antibody lists, clicking ‘Fill list’, reviewing the sequence, and exporting as an .xlsx file.

steps.title: Dispense conjugated antibodies into deepwell plate
steps.instruction: Using the exported worksheet, dispense each FITC, PE, or APC‑conjugated antibody into the specified wells of a 96‑well low‑profile deep‑well plate according to the provided table (e.g., Cycle 1 A1 CD3 REA 115 APC 252 µL, etc.).

steps.title: Set up MACSima experiment and run cycles
steps.instruction: In the MACSima interface, select ‘Experiment Creation’, import the antibody worksheet, choose ‘MACSwell Two’ for the sample rack and a 96‑well low‑profile deep‑well plate for reagents, insert the framed slide and plate, define ROI based on DAPI, configure autofocus (hardware + image‑based), and start the experiment. After completion, open the summary screen to retrieve Calibration, ExperimentDefinition, PreprocessedData, and RawData files.

steps.title: Optional H&E staining after imaging
steps.instruction: Cover tissue with Mayer’s Hematoxylin for 5 min, rinse twice with distilled water, apply Bluing Reagent 10–15 s, rinse, dip in absolute ethanol, stain with Eosin Y for 2–3 min, rinse with absolute ethanol, and dry at 37 °C for 12–18 h (or rinse with ddH₂O 1 min before drying for DAPI‑based mask alignment).

steps.title: Preprocess images in MACS iQ View
steps.instruction: Load ‘RawData’ via ‘Open Raw Directory’, select Nikon 20× Plan Fluor ELWD lens, set exposure to ‘Automatic’ at 100 % scaling, enable ‘Crop to DAPI’, and click ‘Start Preprocessing’. After completion, load the preprocessed image via ‘Project Browser’.

steps.title: Segment cells using advanced morphology
steps.instruction: In the segmentation panel, choose ‘Advanced Morphology for Tissue’ with DAPI as nucleus reference, then select ‘Constrained Donut’ with automatic constraint channels for cytoplasm segmentation.

steps.title: Classify cell phenotypes by gating
steps.instruction: Apply gating‑based classification to identify cell types such as Cytokeratin⁺ tumor cells; CD3⁺CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cells (and their CD45RA/RO sub‑subsets); CD3⁺CD4⁺ helper T cells (and sub‑sets); CD20⁺CD3⁻ B‑cell subsets; CD38⁺ plasma cells; CD57⁺CD107a⁺HLA‑DR⁺ NK cells; CD68⁺HLA‑DR⁺ macrophages; Mast Cell Tryptase⁺; Podoplanin⁺ lymphatic endothelium; CD31⁺ blood vessel endothelium.

steps.title: Perform spatial distance analysis
steps.instruction: In ‘Workflow Editor’, create distance metrics for a chosen cell type (e.g., CTLs); then in ‘Feature Plot’, generate histograms of tumor‑cell distances, categorising as ≤30 µm (close), 30–60 µm (intermediate), and >60 µm ≤ 90 µm (far).

steps.title: Prepare reference (Δ0) sample for MS
steps.instruction: Scrape deparaffinised tissue from PEN membranes into 1.5 mL tubes; add 100 µL 60 mM TEAB + 0.01 % DDM; incubate 1 h at 95 °C (800 × g); centrifuge 1,000 × g 1 min; sonicate 30 s on/30 s off for 12 cycles (high power); add acetonitrile to 12.5 % final; shake 10 s, spin 1,000 × g 1 min; incubate 1 h at 75 °C; cool to 22 °C–26 °C; measure protein (A₂₈₀, NanoDrop or Qubit/BCA); dilute LysC and trypsin 1:50 in 60 mM TEAB + 12 % ACN; add enzymes; digest 12–18 h at 37 °C, 300 rpm; acidify with 1 % TFA; SpeedVac to dryness; reconstitute in 400 µL Buffer A (0.1 % formic acid).

steps.title: Cleanup reference peptides with C18 columns
steps.instruction: Activate C18 columns with 100 µL methanol, centrifuge 750 × g 5 min; equilibrate with 100 µL Buffer B, centrifuge 750 × g 5 min; add 100 µL Buffer A, centrifuge 750 × g 5 min; load sample, wash twice with Buffer A; elute with 100–500 µL 80 % ACN + 0.1 % formic acid; SpeedVac to dryness; reconstitute to 0.125 µg/µL in 60 mM TEAB + 10 % ACN (pH 8.5).

steps.title: Light dimethyl label reference peptides
steps.instruction: Add light formaldehyde to 0.15 % final and light NaBH₃CN to 0.023 M; incubate 1 h at 22 °C–26 °C; add ammonia to 0.13 % final, spin 1,000 × g 1 min, incubate 2 min; acidify with 10 % TFA to 1 % final, spin 1,000 × g 1 min; SpeedVac to dryness. Reconstitute in Buffer A to 1 ng/µL for Evotip loading or store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare experimental (Δ4/Δ8) samples
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL 60 mM TEAB + 0.01 % DDM to each well; seal, centrifuge 2,000 × g 10 min; incubate 95 °C 60 min; cool to 22 °C–26 °C; centrifuge 1,000 × g 10 s; add 1 µL 60 % ACN (final 12 % ACN in 5 µL); seal, centrifuge 1,000 × g 10 s; incubate 75 °C 60 min; cool; add LysC (4 ng total) diluted in 60 mM TEAB + 12 % ACN (4 ng/µL), seal, centrifuge 1,000 × g 10 s, incubate 37 °C 3 h; add trypsin (6 ng total) diluted similarly (4 ng/µL), seal, centrifuge 1,000 × g 10 s, incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Dimethyl label experimental samples
steps.instruction: For Δ4 (intermediate) add 1.5 % CD₂O formaldehyde; for Δ8 (heavy) add 1.5 % ¹³CD₂O; add 0.23 M NaBH₃CN (light) or 0.23 M NaBD₃CN (heavy) to reach 0.023 M; seal and incubate 1 h at 22 °C–26 °C; add 1.43 % ammonia to reach 0.13 % final, spin 1,000 × g 1 min, incubate 2 min; add 10 % TFA to reach 1 % final, spin 1,000 × g 1 min.

steps.title: Load samples onto Evotips for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Wash Evotips with 20 µL Buffer B (99.9 % ACN, 0.1 % FA) at 700 × g 1 min; activate in 2‑propanol 1 min, spin 700 × g 1 min; wash with 20 µL Buffer A (0.1 % FA) at 700 × g 1 min; load 25 ng Δ0 peptides, then Δ4 and Δ8 on the same tip, centrifuge 700 × g 1 min; rinse wells with 20 µL Buffer A and load rinse onto tip, centrifuge 700 × g 1 min; overlay tip with 100 µL Buffer A and centrifuge 700 × g 10 s. Evotips are now ready for LC‑MS.

steps.title: Generate spectral library with FragPipe
steps.instruction: Run FragPipe v18.0 (MSFragger v3.5, Philosopher v4.4.0, EasyPQP v0.1.3) against the human FASTA (2023, UP000005640_9606) using DIA_SpecLib_Quant workflow with fixed N‑terminal and lysine dimethyl (+28.0313 Da), variable Met oxidation, no carbamidomethylation, up to 1 missed cleavage, precursor charge 2–4, peptide mass 300–1800 Da, length 7–30 aa.

steps.title: Analyze DIA data with DIA‑NN
steps.instruction: Process DIA raw files in DIA‑NN v1.8.1 with the generated library, setting fixed dimethyl modification (28.0313 Da, nK), defining channels (light 0, intermediate 4, heavy 8) with respective mass shifts, enabling isotopologue matching, MBR, heuristic protein inference, and other listed parameters.

steps.title: Post‑process DIA results and quantify proteins
steps.instruction: Filter DIA‑NN output using RefQuant (Lib.PG.Q.Value < 0.01, Q.value < 0.01, Channel.Q.Value < 0.15); then consolidate protein groups with MaxLFQ via the R iq package (preprocess, create protein list, create protein table) and export as a tab‑delimited result file.

description: This protocol presents multiplexed imaging-powered Deep Visual Proteomics (mipDVP), a spatially resolved workflow integrating cyclic 22-plex immunofluorescence imaging, automated laser microdissection, and high-sensitivity mass spectrometry to dissect the proteomic landscape of tonsil cancer microenvironments.1 The method subjects formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) tissues to automated cyclic staining and imaging using the MACSima platform, combined with single-cell isolation using the Leica LMD7, thus enabling precise spatial mapping of tumor and immune cell populations. By coupling the Evosep One liquid chromatography (LC) system with the timsTOF SCP mass spectrometry, the method achieves deep proteome coverage from minimal input, capturing cell-type-specific functional states and intercellular interactions. Optimized for tumor-immune crosstalk, this reproducible framework bridges spatial biology with proteomic depth, offering insights into microenvironmental heterogeneity. While optimized for tonsil cancer, we have validated the protocol in colorectal cancer microenvironments.1
